title: Global shortcut for 'Minimize All' doesn't work well with the respective applet
line: The Minimize All Windows widget and the Meta+Shift+D shortcut can now undo each other.
explanation: The Minimize All Windows widget and KWin's optional Minimize All script (Meta+Shift+D) each kept a private list of the windows they had minimized. After the shortcut, the widget found nothing to minimize, marked itself active with an empty list and restored nothing; after the widget, the shortcut found none of its own windows and only brought back the window it re-activated. When the KWin script is loaded, the widget now toggles through it (kglobalaccel invokeShortcut MinimizeAll), so both share KWin's state, and its Restore/Minimize tooltip follows whether all windows on the current desktop and activity are minimized. Without the script, the widget behaves as before.

commits.message:
applets/minimizeall: share state with KWin's Minimize All script

The applet and KWin's Minimize All shortcut each remembered only the
windows they had minimized themselves, so one could not undo the other.
When that script is loaded, the applet now triggers it to toggle instead.

BUG: 420460

review.text: The diagnosis is right: the applet and KWin's minimizeall script each keep a private list. But the fix couples the applet to the script's internal shortcut name through kglobalaccel invokeShortcut, and adds a D-Bus round trip on every click. The applet's 'active' state is also wrong until the async isScriptLoaded reply arrives, and it never updates if the script is enabled or disabled later. The two would really share state through an API in KWin, not by pressing the shortcut on the user's behalf.
changes: Fix it in KWin: have the minimizeall script (or KWin itself) expose a proper D-Bus toggle/state interface that the applet uses, or have the applet own the logic and the shortcut call it, so there is one implementation instead of invoking a global shortcut by name.
If the coupling stays, track script load/unload instead of polling once at startup and on click.
